propositions: A store write that cannot acquire the write lock within its timeout is permanently discarded with no retry or queue, causing data loss when holder duration exceeds the budget.

The acquire() budget is computed as a single deadline across all attempts, with both fcntl and mkdir legs polling non-blocking with jitter, resulting in no fairness and lottery-like behavior among waiters.

Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() converts write loss into latency by re-attempting acquisition across discrete passes (retries=2 default, ~181.5s total) with exponential backoff and per-pass warnings, never replaying the write body.

Five call sites explicitly opt into retries via retries=_write_path_retries() reading REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env var (default 2, clamped [0,10]), while all other callers retain fail-fast via the retries=0 default.

Writes that first fail within one 60s pass are re-attempted and succeed on later passes as measured latency rather than terminal loss, verified in reproduction test with real subprocess holders and confirmed against live Jira DC integration.

The retry mechanism is safe from double-append because the retry loop lives strictly inside acquire() before any caller body executes, so LockTimeout is raised before staging or committing, preventing phantom-write semantics.
